The Data Science internship in short

In the SkillMe Data Science internship you build one of 3 projects, such as InsightHub: Interactive Data Intelligence & ML Dashboard, a project where you explore a real-world dataset, clean it up, build a simple prediction model, and finish with a small interactive dashboard. In week 1 you load the classic Titanic dataset into pandas and explore it: what columns exist, what is missing, and what basic patterns show up. By week 4 you turn your analysis and model into an interactive Streamlit dashboard that anyone can explore in a browser, and write a clear README that tells the story of your project. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the Data Science internship covers

Shown for InsightHub: Interactive Data Intelligence & ML Dashboard. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Explore a Dataset with Pandas

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Load the classic Titanic dataset into pandas and explore it: what columns exist, what is missing, and what basic patterns show up. This is the foundation every data science project starts from, and it builds comfort with pandas and simple charts.

    What you learn

    • Loading data with pandas.read_csv and inspecting it with .head(), .info(), .describe()
    • Selecting, filtering and grouping data with pandas
    • Finding missing values with .isnull().sum()
    • Making basic charts with matplotlib or seaborn

    What you submit

    • A notebook that loads and explores the Titanic dataset
    • At least two clear charts (bar chart and histogram, or similar)
    • A short written summary of your findings in markdown
    • A README explaining how to open and run the notebook
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • The notebook runs top to bottom without errors
    • .isnull().sum() output correctly identifies the columns with missing data
    • At least two charts are visible in the notebook with titles and axis labels
    • The written summary references actual numbers from your analysis

    Stretch goal: Add a heatmap of correlations between numeric columns using seaborn.heatmap(df.corr()).

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Clean Data and Engineer Features

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Clean the missing and messy values you found last week and create a few new columns that make the data more useful for analysis or modeling. This is the unglamorous but essential skill of turning raw data into something usable.

    What you learn

    • Handling missing values with .fillna() and .dropna()
    • Creating new columns from existing ones (feature engineering)
    • Converting categories to numbers with pandas.get_dummies or label encoding
    • Detecting outliers with boxplots and simple thresholds

    What you submit

    • A clean_data(df) function that handles missing values
    • At least two engineered feature columns
    • One-hot or label-encoded categorical columns
    • A saved titanic_clean.csv file
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • clean_data(df).isnull().sum() shows zero missing values in the columns you chose to clean
    • The new feature columns (family_size, is_alone) contain correct, sensible values
    • The categorical columns are numeric after encoding
    • titanic_clean.csv loads back into pandas with the expected shape and columns

    Stretch goal: Bucket age into groups (child, teen, adult, senior) using pandas.cut and compare survival rate across the buckets.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Train a Prediction Model with scikit-learn

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Use your cleaned dataset to train a simple machine learning model that predicts survival, and evaluate how good it really is. This is your first hands-on experience with the standard scikit-learn workflow used across most ML projects.

    What you learn

    • Splitting data into train and test sets with train_test_split
    • Training a classifier such as LogisticRegression or RandomForestClassifier
    • Evaluating a model with accuracy, precision, recall and a confusion matrix
    • Avoiding data leakage by fitting transformations only on training data

    What you submit

    • A train/test split with a fixed random_state for reproducibility
    • Two trained models (logistic regression and random forest) with evaluation metrics
    • A short comparison table or printout of accuracy, precision and recall for both
    • A saved model file (model.joblib or similar)
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • The train/test split does not mix rows between the two sets
    • Both models train and produce predictions on the test set without errors
    • Accuracy, precision, recall and a confusion matrix are printed for both models
    • The saved model file can be reloaded with joblib.load and still makes predictions

    Stretch goal: Use GridSearchCV to tune the random forest's n_estimators and max_depth and see if it improves the test accuracy.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Streamlit Dashboard and Write-Up

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Turn your analysis and model into an interactive Streamlit dashboard that anyone can explore in a browser, and write a clear README that tells the story of your project. This is where your work becomes something you can actually show people.

    What you learn

    • Building an interactive app with Streamlit widgets and layout
    • Loading a saved model and making live predictions from user input
    • Displaying charts and tables inside a Streamlit app
    • Writing a project README that tells a clear data story

    What you submit

    • A working Streamlit app (app.py) with charts and a live prediction form
    • A model loaded from disk and used for real-time predictions
    • requirements.txt and a complete README telling the project's data story
    • A 30-60 second demo video
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • streamlit run app.py opens a working dashboard in the browser
    • Changing the input widgets changes the predicted outcome and probability
    • The dashboard shows at least one chart from your earlier analysis
    • A new person can set up and run the dashboard using only the README

    Stretch goal: Add a page that lets a user upload their own CSV of passengers and see predictions for all of them in a table.

Data Science internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the Data Science internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: InsightHub: Interactive Data Intelligence & ML Dashboard, FinanceForecaster: Algorithmic Market & Crypto Trend Engine or SurveyLens: Public Survey & Opinion Data Explorer. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Data Science internship?

The Data Science internship works with Python, SQL and Data Viz. Week 1: loading data with pandas.read_csv and inspecting it with .head(), .info(), .describe(); selecting, filtering and grouping data with pandas. Week 2: handling missing values with .fillna() and .dropna(); creating new columns from existing ones (feature engineering). Week 3: splitting data into train and test sets with train_test_split; training a classifier such as LogisticRegression or RandomForestClassifier. Week 4: building an interactive app with Streamlit widgets and layout; loading a saved model and making live predictions from user input.

Do I need experience to apply for the Data Science internship?

You need the basics of Python, SQL and Data Viz, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you load the classic Titanic dataset into pandas and explore it: what columns exist, what is missing, and what basic patterns show up. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Data Science milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of InsightHub: Interactive Data Intelligence & ML Dashboard, that means: the notebook runs top to bottom without errors; .isnull().sum() output correctly identifies the columns with missing data; at least two charts are visible in the notebook with titles and axis labels; the written summary references actual numbers from your analysis. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Data Science internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Explored the Titanic dataset using pandas, groupby and descriptive statistics; Identified missing data and survival patterns by class and sex; Built my first data visualizations with matplotlib and seaborn; Cleaned missing values in a real dataset with a documented, repeatable strategy; Engineered new features like family size to improve analysis; Encoded categorical data and saved a clean dataset for modeling; Trained logistic regression and random forest models to predict Titanic survival; Evaluated models with accuracy, precision, recall and a confusion matrix; Compared feature importance across models to understand what drove predictions; Built an interactive Streamlit dashboard for my Titanic survival analysis; Connected a trained scikit-learn model to live user input for real-time predictions; Wrote a complete project README telling the full data story from raw data to dashboard.

What are the other projects in the Data Science internship?

FinanceForecaster: Algorithmic Market & Crypto Trend Engine: Pull real stock price data, explore trends, build a simple forecasting model, and finish with an interactive dashboard (not financial advice). SurveyLens: Public Survey & Opinion Data Explorer: Explore a real public survey dataset, clean and summarise it, and build a small interactive dashboard that tells its story. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the Data Science internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based and goes to the interns whose reviewed Data Science work stands out in their cohort, not to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
